Trumpet gentians so deep blue-violet they look poured from a bottle, growing flat and tight against the ground, each one banked hard against a grey slab as though the rock is holding them in place.

Dense round clumps of tiny hot-pink flowers spread flat on the stone where moss campion has sealed every gap between boulders, and starry saxifrage with small white flowers with red dots wedges into the remaining cracks.

Glacier buttercups, small and yellow, opening in the first bare inch of ground where snowmelt has just pulled back, and alpine snowbells hanging violet fringed bells above them, both pressed low against the wet gravel.

Purple saxifrage spreading bright magenta flat over the rock face in one unbroken sheet, and yellow mountain saxifrage with small yellow orange-speckled flowers filling the seams below, the whole slab burning with colour.

Indian paintbrush in scarlet flame-shaped spikes no higher than a hand, crowded on the lee side of a granite boulder, and dwarf rhododendron shrubs with small magenta-pink bell flowers in dense low clumps ringing the stone's base.

A single slope solid with alpine lupine, the blue-violet spikes packed in short stiff rows, every plant the same height as the stones between them, the whole hillside one flat continuous colour with no gap and no tall stem.

White mountain anemones with gold centres growing in dense low clumps pressed against the uphill face of a slab, and edelweiss with white woolly star-shaped heads flat and tight beside them, filling every pocket of grit between rocks.
Alpine primula in deep magenta-pink with a yellow centre, in dense round clumps hugging the ground out of the wind, ringing a half-buried stone so tightly they look set there on purpose.

Pasqueflowers in furry purple bells with silver-haired stems pushing up through last year's dead brown stems, banked against a frost-cracked slab, each furry stalk no taller than the surrounding broken rock.

Alpine forget-me-nots in sky blue with a small gold centre growing flat and tight across a gravel slope, and spring gentians in intense sky-blue pressed into cracks between them, the combined blue so saturated the grey stone behind them looks almost black.

Short thick-stemmed alpine sunflowers every head facing exactly the same direction, in dense low clumps along the windward edge of a boulder field, each stem stiff and thick as a finger, shorter than the rocks beside them.

Alpine aster with violet petals and a gold centre and alpine bellflower with small nodding violet bell-shaped flowers crowded together on the lee side of a slab, both in tight low growth with no stem rising above the surrounding stone.

Golden-yellow mountain daisies in short stiff spikes a hand high ringing a frost-shattered boulder, and alpine buttercups in round butter-yellow flat between the loose stones beside them, the combined yellow reading like something spilled.

Starry saxifrage with small white flowers with red dots pressed into every crack and seam across a vertical rock face, and purple saxifrage spreading bright magenta flat across the ledges below, the two species dividing the stone between them.

Spring gentians in intense sky-blue and trumpet gentians in deep blue-violet growing flat and tight together against the same grey slab, two blues so close in hue they blur at the border, banked hard against the rock out of the wind.

Alpine bistort with white bottlebrush heads on wiry stems in short stiff growth a hand high, and white dryad flowers with gold centres hugging the ground between loose stones, both crowded into the sheltered hollow behind a boulder.

Fireweed in tall magenta spikes — the tallest plants in this entire frame — rising from a rubble slope and immediately showing how everything else here is pressed flat, the spikes absurd in their height against the surrounding stone.

Alpine toadflax in violet and cream pressed into cracks in a near-vertical slab, and yellow mountain saxifrage in small yellow orange-speckled flowers filling the seams beside them, the two species together covering every gap in the rock face.

Dense round clumps of tiny hot-pink flowers spread flat on the stone where moss campion fills a broad granite shelf, and alpine snowbells hanging nodding violet bells at the shelf's edge, fringed petals catching the air above bare rock.

Edelweiss in white woolly star-shaped heads flat against a grey slab, and alpine forget-me-nots in sky blue with a small gold centre packed into the grit beside them, white against grey and blue against white, three colours total and nothing muted.

Dwarf rhododendron shrubs with small magenta-pink bell flowers in dense low clumps and Indian paintbrush in scarlet flame-shaped spikes growing together on the lee side of a boulder field, the combined hot colour violent against bare broken rock.

Glacier buttercups in small yellow at the snow edge and pasqueflowers in furry purple bells with silver-haired stems pushing up through grit just metres back from the snow line, both plants so low and tight they seem part of the ground itself.

Alpine lupine in blue-violet spikes and alpine aster in violet petals with gold centres packed together in dense low growth ringing a half-buried boulder, the combined blue-violet mass filling every gap between stone and bare gravel.

Alpine primula in deep magenta-pink with a yellow centre filling the seams between frost-split slabs, and white mountain anemones with gold centres banked against the same slabs above them, the bright magenta below and white above making the stone look framed.

Yellow mountain saxifrage in small yellow orange-speckled flowers and alpine buttercups in round butter-yellow crowded into the loose gravel on the lee side of a boulder, both flat and tight, both shorter than the stones beside them, the ground all yellow and grey with nothing between.
